_source: Answers drawn only from rules the platform enforces — app_config, fees.json, plans.json, riders.json, lifecycle.json and the services each of those names. If a rule changes there, change the answer here.
_fields: audience picks the Help Centre tab (customers, shops, riders, general). home: true also puts the question on the home page.

items.q: Where does QuickLocal deliver?
items.a: {city} for now. You see shops within {radius} km by default, and you can widen that to 8, 12, 16 or {maxRadius} km for each saved address. Nothing beyond {maxRadius} km can be ordered, so search never shows you a shop that cannot reach you.

items.q: How long does an order take?
items.a: Never more than {hours} hours — that ceiling is set on every order, and if one runs late you are told. Most arrive much sooner, because the shop is a few streets away.

items.q: What does delivery cost?
items.a: A flat {base} base covers the first {freeKm} km. Beyond that, a per-km charge derived from the day's fuel price is added. Cross the shop's free-delivery threshold and the shop pays the base instead of you. The estimator on the home page works out any order to the rupee.

items.q: Are there hidden charges?
items.a: No. You pay for your basket and your share of delivery, and both are shown before you pay. Nothing is added at the door.

items.q: Which aisles can I shop?
items.a: {aisleList}. Each is a fixed category in the app, with its own look.

items.q: Why does the rider ask me for a code?
items.a: An order is only marked delivered when you give the rider the one-time code from your app — so nothing is ever delivered on a tap.

items.q: What if no rider takes my order?
items.a: Once the shop accepts, riders nearby are offered the job one at a time, and each chooses whether to take it. If nobody accepts within fifteen minutes, the order is cancelled and refunded automatically.

items.q: What happens if something goes wrong?
items.a: An order can be cancelled before pickup and anything authorised is released. Refunds are raised against the original payment and marked done only once Razorpay has accepted them, and complaints are escalated rather than closed quietly.

items.q: What if I do not finish paying?
items.a: An order that is never paid is cancelled after thirty minutes and its stock goes back on the shelf, so it holds nothing up for anyone.

items.q: How does Refer & Earn work?
items.a: Share your code. When a friend's first order qualifies, ₹{referral} comes off your next one. The amount is set by the platform, so it is the same for everybody.

items.q: How much does it cost to list a shop?
items.a: Listing is free for up to {freeProducts} products. Starter is ₹{starterPrice} a month for {starterProducts}, Growth ₹{growthPrice} for {growthProducts}, and Pro ₹{proPrice} for unlimited. Change or cancel any month.

items.q: What is a free-delivery threshold?
items.a: The basket size above which you cover the {base} delivery base, so the customer sees free delivery. It is {threshold} until you set your own, per category.

items.q: When does a shop get paid?
items.a: After every delivered order, straight to your bank or UPI, reconciled automatically. Never before the order is delivered.

items.q: What documents does a shop need?
items.a: Aadhaar, PAN, bank proof, a shop licence and two photographs of the shop — outside and inside. A bank account or UPI id and a finished profile come first, and the app names exactly what is still missing.

items.q: How are riders paid?
items.a: You are paid the order's whole delivery fee: {base} for any trip up to {freeKm} km, plus about ₹{perKm} for every kilometre beyond it at the day's fuel price — paid after every delivered order.

items.q: Can I deliver on a bicycle?
items.a: Yes. A bicycle needs no licence, registration or number plate — just your Aadhaar, PAN, bank proof and three photographs of the bike. A motorbike, scooter, auto or CNG auto also needs a driving licence and its registration certificate.

items.q: Can I be given an order I do not want?
items.a: No. A job only reaches you after the shop has accepted the order, and it arrives as an offer — the shop, the customer, both distances and what it pays. You have a minute to accept or decline; decline, or let it pass, and it goes to the next rider. Nothing is assigned to you until you say yes.

items.q: How do the tiers work?
items.a: Bronze from your first day; Silver at 50 deliveries and 3.5 stars; Gold at 200 and 4.0; Platinum at 500 and 4.5. Tiers only ever move up on their own — a dip in rating never demotes you overnight.

items.q: Can I take two jobs at once?
items.a: No — one active delivery at a time, so a customer's order is never riding around behind somebody else's.

items.q: What if I cannot collect an order in time?
items.a: Once you accept, you have thirty minutes to collect. After that the job is released to another rider rather than left waiting, and you are free to take the next one.

items.q: When will the apps be in the stores?
items.a: Soon. The listings are not published yet, which is why the store buttons say so instead of linking to a page that does not exist. Leave your email at the foot of the home page and we will tell you the day they land.

items.q: Why are there no customer numbers on this site?
items.a: Because we are early, and a figure like 50,000 customers would be a claim our own database contradicts. Every number here is a rule the platform enforces, not a boast.

items.q: What are events?
items.a: Occasions — a festival, a seasonal sale, late-night deals — that appear as a tab right after All in the app, with their own page of offers. Each has a window, and the tab leaves on its own when it ends.

items.q: How do offers work?
items.a: Shops set them on one product, a whole aisle or everything they sell — a percentage or a flat amount, sometimes above a minimum order or with a cap on the saving. Every offer is dated and applied at checkout while it runs; there is no code to type.

items.q: Can I choose which notifications I get?
items.a: Yes. Offers, marketing and updates can each be switched off in the app. Messages about your orders, delivery, payments and security always come through.

items.q: When can I rate an order?
items.a: Once it is delivered, for seven days. You can rate the shop and the rider, once each per order.
